original_question.question:
Each of the three large squares shown below is the same size. In I and II, $P$, $Q$, $R$ and $S$ lie one third of a side from the bottom-left, bottom-right, top-right and top-left corners respectively, and consecutive points are joined; I also draws $PR$. In III, $U$ is one third of a side from the bottom-left corner and $V$ is two thirds of a side above the bottom-right corner. How do the shaded areas of these squares compare?

Choices:
A: $S_{I} = S_{II} = S_{III}$
B: $S_{I} = S_{II} > S_{III}$
C: $S_{III} > S_{I} > S_{II}$
D: $S_{II} = S_{III} > S_{I}$
E: $S_{I} > S_{II} = S_{III}$
